skim: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake off Indonesia's Flores Island killed at least two and triggered a tsunami warning for over 500,000 residents who felt the shaking.
Trump says he will declare the Strait of Hormuz “a territory of the United States” as tensions with Iran escalate over the vital oil chokepoint.
Anthropic is reportedly eyeing a $2 trillion valuation for an October IPO, which would top SpaceX's record $1.77 trillion debut.
Modi marked India's 80th Independence Day from the Red Fort with a new “Viksit Bharat” growth agenda, as Chamoli's flooded tunnel rescue continued nearby.
Wall Street's rally cooled on weak US retail sales data and a 6% Broadcom slide, even as the S&P 500 notched a third straight weekly gain.

stories.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Indonesia's Flores Island triggers tsunami warning
stories.body: A 7.7-magnitude quake struck 68km northwest of Ende off Flores Island at a shallow 10km depth, killing two people at Maumere port and injuring one, with three strong aftershocks (up to M6.1) within 30 minutes, per Al Jazeera (Aug 15). Indonesia's disaster agency BNPB issued a tsunami warning, with official Abdul Muhari urging residents to “move away from the shore, either by going more than two kilometres inland or by moving up into hilly areas more than 10 metres high”; over 500,000 people on Flores felt very strong shaking.

stories.headline: Colombia earthquake toll climbs to 281 as 379 remain missing
stories.body: The death toll from the Aug 11 M7.4 quake centered near San Jose del Palmar in Chocó rose to 281 confirmed dead with 379 still missing and nearly 3,971 injured, per Türkiye Today (Aug 14). Rescue teams continue searching collapsed buildings for survivors, though authorities say the chances of finding people alive are decreasing; the disaster has destroyed homes, schools and hospitals across several cities, with tremors felt as far as Bogotá.

stories.headline: Europe's heat crisis deepens: 12,500 dead in Germany, homes destroyed by UK wildfires
stories.body: Germany has recorded 12,500 heat-related deaths since Jan 1 — already surpassing all of 2018 — while West London hit 38.1C, its hottest day of the year, per Graham Media Group/Click2Houston (Aug 14). Wildfires destroyed 20-30 homes in Stourbridge, England, hospitalizing 19 people and six firefighters; France evacuated 500+ from Landes and shut six nuclear reactors, Croatia saw one death and 1,000+ evacuated near Omiš, and evacuee Jane Baxter recalled: “They thought the fire was changing directions, and they didn't know which direction it was going in.”

stories.headline: Record rainfall kills 8 in Chiba, Japan; heaviest daily total since 1966
stories.body: The Japan Meteorological Agency formally named the disaster the “August 2026 Chiba Heavy Rain” after 351mm fell in a single day on Aug 13 — the highest since 1966 — including 115mm in one hour, breaking the prior record of 71mm, per Watchers.news (Aug 14). Eight people have died across Chiba City, Ichikawa, Kashiwa, Sakura and Yachiyo, with 7,359 people sheltering at 359 sites, railway lines suspended and an expressway closed by a landslide.

stories.headline: Zambia election disputed as opposition claims victory before official results
stories.body: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile declared victory over incumbent Hakainde Hichilema based on his party's parallel vote tabulation, alleging irregularities including military control of tallying centers and missing electoral forms, per AllAfrica (Aug 14). Hichilema stopped short of conceding or claiming victory, saying “we continue to receive encouraging results and reports of peace, unity and solidarity across our country as the votes come in,” while Mundubile insisted “the people of Zambia voted. Their decision must be respected.”

stories.headline: Barcelona gives itself 48 hours to land Rodri
stories.body: Barcelona have set themselves a 48-hour deadline to close the Rodri deal, planning to unveil the World Cup Golden Ball winner at their Joan Gamper Trophy presentation if terms are struck in time. Manchester City is holding out for roughly €80m while Barça's latest offer sits at €60m plus €10m in add-ons, leaving the sides deadlocked, with City reportedly eyeing Chelsea's Enzo Fernández as a replacement, per Yahoo Sports (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Gill's India settles on three left-arm spinners for Galle opener
stories.body: With Jasprit Bumrah and Sai Sudharsan sidelined, India are set to field three left-arm spinners — Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav and uncapped Manav Suthar — behind a Prasidh Krishna-Mohammed Siraj new-ball pairing as the series opener gets underway at Galle. Captain Shubman Gill confirmed Krishna will share the new ball with Siraj, while Devdutt Padikkal comes in at No.3 for the injured Sudharsan, per The Week (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Manchester Super Giants join Trent Rockets in Hundred men's final
stories.body: Paul Walter's 80 off 46 balls and a 114-run stand with Heinrich Klaasen powered Manchester Super Giants to a 20-run Eliminator win over SunRisers Leeds, with Josh Tongue's 4-26 sealing it; they now face table-toppers Trent Rockets at Lord's on Sunday. In the women's competition SunRisers Leeds beat Southern Brave by five wickets to set up their own final against Trent Rockets, with Super Giants captain Jos Buttler saying, “So many players stood up in some crucial moments — Paul Walter has been incredible,” per Sky Sports (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Ferrari's Monza upgrade could double Hamilton's power gain
stories.body: Ferrari's second ADUO engine upgrade, expected at Monza, is projected to deliver around 15 horsepower — double the roughly 7hp gain from the earlier Austria update — worth an estimated two tenths of a second per lap. “With the first half, it has been amazing given I think we've been probably like three or four tenths down on the straights in pace and power … I think the second half will be stronger,” Hamilton said, per GPFans (Aug 13).

stories.headline: Antonelli holds 50-point lead over Hamilton as F1 returns
stories.body: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 drivers' championship on 219 points, 50 clear of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton on 169, with George Russell (160) and Charles Leclerc (138) also in the mix as the title race resumes with 11 rounds left. “F1 is about to emerge from its summer break and guess what — we have ourselves a title race,” wrote GPFans consultant editor Graham Shaw (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Wall Street's rally cools as weak retail data hits stocks, Broadcom sinks 6%
stories.body: The S&P 500 slipped 0.17% to 7,785.76, the Dow fell 107.58 points to 53,732.41, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.28% to 26,729.16 on Friday after July retail sales fell 0.6% month-over-month, reviving worries about consumer health, per The Motley Fool (Aug 14). Broadcom tumbled 6% to $392.99 after Bank of America analysts questioned a potential $370 billion debt-financing vehicle tied to its AI infrastructure buildout, while Reddit surged 13% on news of its S&P 500 inclusion and the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.69%. Despite the pullback, the index still closed out its third straight week of gains, extending Thursday's record high on cooling-inflation optimism.

stories.headline: Workday's $43B Silver Lake buyout talks deepen, echoing EA-style take-private playbook
stories.body: Shares of Workday surged as much as 18% to close near $206 on Thursday after Reuters reported Silver Lake is in advanced talks to take the HR-software maker private at a roughly $43 billion valuation, following months of quiet contact between the two sides, per Axios (Aug 14) and Benzinga (Aug 13). Axios Pro Deals analyst Chris Metinko said the potential deal “indicates Silver Lake believes large systems of record are less vulnerable to AI disruption, given they're ingrained in enterprises, hard to replicate, and can leverage data for AI initiatives,” and noted Silver Lake may bring in co-investors similar to its $55 billion Electronic Arts take-private with Saudi Arabia's PIF and Affinity Partners. Workday stock had been down roughly 15% in 2026 and more than 40% below its 2024 peak before the report broke.

stories.headline: Databricks' $5B round draws $15B in demand as AI “token bills” spook CFOs
stories.body: Databricks closed its $5 billion funding round at a $190 billion valuation after investors offered as much as $15 billion, with the AI data company reporting a $7 billion annualized revenue run-rate, 80% year-over-year growth, and 12 straight months of positive adjusted free cash flow, per Tech Times (Aug 14). Coatue Management led the round, joined by Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price, Sixth Street, TPG, Clearlake Capital, Point72 and existing backers including Andreessen Horowitz and Goldman Sachs; CEO Ali Ghodsi said surging AI usage costs mean “this token maxing has freaked out the CFOs,” driving demand for Databricks' infrastructure tools.

stories.headline: Brent crude rebounds to $89.53 as Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks keep supply risk elevated
stories.body: Brent crude eased slightly on the day to $89.53 a barrel Friday (-0.83%) but sits nearly 7% higher than a month ago and up more than 33% year-on-year, per Fortune (Aug 14), reversing course from earlier in the week as attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Gulf states keep a geopolitical risk premium in the market. The renewed volatility follows a string of incidents this month, including an Iranian strike on an ADNOC tanker that the UAE and Qatar condemned, and a Houthi claim to have hit a Saudi oil tanker.

stories.headline: Gold hovers near $4,400 as traders bet the Fed holds rates steady in September
stories.body: Gold traded around $4,400-$4,420 an ounce Friday morning before closing the session near $4,373, per Yahoo Finance and The Motley Fool (Aug 14), staying just below the psychological $4,400 level it slipped under earlier in the week. Cooling inflation data has pushed CME-tracked odds of the Fed holding rates steady in September to 69.4%, and gold — which “does not pay interest” — tends to benefit when rate-hike expectations fade, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 14); separately, the Treasury's 30-year bond auction priced at 5.216%, its highest yield in 25 years.

stories.headline: Anthropic eyes $2 trillion valuation for October IPO
stories.body: Investors expect Anthropic to go public in October at a valuation of $2 trillion or more, which would top SpaceX's record $1.77 trillion IPO from June, per Fortune (Aug 14). The figure has more than doubled from $965 billion after May's Series H, with Q2 2026 revenue reportedly more than doubling to $10.9 billion and the company posting an operating profit for the first time — though Fortune notes it would need $59-79 billion in annual profit to justify the valuation on typical tech multiples, having filed confidentially with the SEC in June.

stories.headline: OpenAI's revenue run rate tops $40 billion ahead of IPO
stories.body: OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate has doubled from roughly $20 billion in late 2025 to more than $40 billion, with monthly revenue up over 20% in July alone, per Bloomberg (Aug 13). Co-founder Greg Brockman cited subscriptions, the Codex coding agent, ChatGPT Work and early advertising efforts as growth drivers as the company preps for an eventual IPO and races Anthropic, which reported a $47 billion run rate in May.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash, undercutting its own three-week-old model by 50%
stories.body: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after 3.6 Flash, jumping from 34.4% to 43.6% on the FrontierCode coding benchmark and from 49.0% to 65.3% on DeepSWE, while cutting prices to $0.75/million input and $3.75/million output tokens — half the prior Flash cost, locked through year-end, per The Decoder (Aug 13). Google credited “awesome algorithmic improvements” for the gains, and says the model now beats Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra on its internal measurements, positioning it as the workhorse for coding agents.

stories.headline: DeepSeek launches V4 Pro, then hikes API prices by up to 1,100%
stories.body: DeepSeek shipped an upgraded V4 Pro model and open-sourced its agent software, but will raise API prices starting Aug 16: V4-Pro output tokens jump from $0.87 to $3.96/million at peak hours (up 355%), with some workloads seeing increases as high as 1,100%, per Quartz (Aug 13). The company introduced peak/off-peak pricing (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) to spread developer load, saying it wants “to allocate resources more reasonably,” though even the new rates remain far below Anthropic's Claude 5 pricing of $50/million output tokens.

stories.headline: Apple builds its own China-specific AI model with Alibaba's help
stories.body: Apple has trained a proprietary large language model for the Chinese market to power Apple Intelligence, a shift from relying solely on third-party domestic models, per MacRumors (Aug 14). Alibaba supported development, making Apple reportedly the first foreign company approved by Chinese regulators to offer its own AI model there; Apple briefly published — then pulled — a support guide on connecting Alibaba's Qwen to Siri, with China rollout expected in the coming months.

stories.headline: Trump vows to declare Strait of Hormuz US “territory”
stories.body: Speaking in New York on Friday, Trump escalated the standoff with Tehran: “After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.” Control of the waterway, which carries roughly a fifth of global oil supply, has been the core sticking point since a June US-Iran memorandum broke down; Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi shot back, “The Strait of Hormuz cannot be taken over by a tweet, nor by an aircraft carrier,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 14-15).

stories.headline: Kushner heads to Israel as Netanyahu rejects Gaza disarmament plan
stories.body: Jared Kushner will travel to Israel and Egypt alongside Tony Blair and Nickolay Mladenov after Netanyahu balked at the Trump-backed Board of Peace plan requiring Hamas to disarm and hand weapons to a third party while Israel withdraws from Gaza; a Board of Peace official said “what is critical is that we both agree on the desired outcome and are finding ways to accelerate progress,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 14). The trip follows Thursday's drone strike that killed Gaza City police chief Col. Jamal Abu Kamil, pushing the post-ceasefire Palestinian death toll past 1,250.

stories.headline: Ukraine claims Dnipropetrovsk gains as Russian missile barrages intensify
stories.body: Kyiv says it has recaptured 745 sq km and liberated 26 settlements in a Dnipropetrovsk offensive this year (the Institute for the Study of War puts it at a more conservative 627 sq km), with former commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskii saying the operation “proved that the Ukrainian army is capable not only of steadfastly holding its defences, but also of launching offensives,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 14). Russia fired 198 ballistic and hypersonic missiles in July alone, and its monthly casualties hit nearly 43,000 that month, the highest since January 2025.

stories.headline: Sudan's Blue Nile war deepens as RSF seizes Geisan
stories.body: UN deputy spokesman Farhan Haq said clashes as RSF and allied SPLM-N forces seized Geisan town killed more than 20 civilians and displaced roughly 2,500 people, while drone strikes hit a water station in El Obeid, North Kordofan — a strike the UN called “particularly concerning at a time when access to clean water remains one of the most pressing challenges facing the city,” per Sudan Tribune (Aug 12-14). Sudan's 2026 humanitarian appeal remains 41% underfunded, with only $1.2 billion of the requested $2.9 billion received.

stories.headline: Putin and Kim affirm deepening Russia-North Korea security ties
stories.body: Putin sent a message to Kim Jong Un asserting Moscow and Pyongyang “were cooperating across all areas and coordinating efforts to ensure regional security and stability,” and predicted continued “constructive joint work” on bilateral and international matters, according to North Korean state media KCNA, per Arab News (Aug 15). The exchange, made as Kim laid a wreath honoring Soviet WWII soldiers, underscores an alliance Kyiv says has funneled North Korean missiles and troops into Russia's war on Ukraine.

fixtures.headline: India-Sri Lanka series opener begins at Galle
fixtures.body: The first Test of India's tour gets underway at Galle International Stadium on Saturday, August 15, with play starting 10am IST and the match scheduled through August 19.

fixtures.headline: Hundred Finals Day at Lord's
fixtures.body: Trent Rockets face Manchester Super Giants in the men's final and SunRisers Leeds in the women's final at Lord's on Sunday, with singer Ella Eyre performing; a reserve day is set for Monday.

fixtures.headline: F1 returns from break at Zandvoort for the Dutch Grand Prix
fixtures.body: Practice and sprint qualifying open the weekend Friday August 21, with the sprint race and qualifying Saturday and the Grand Prix itself on Sunday August 23 — the season's first race since the summer break.

fixtures.headline: Premier League 2026/27 season kicks off
fixtures.body: The new season opens August 21-24, headlined by defending champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry City on the opening day, with Newcastle-Liverpool and Fulham-Chelsea among the weekend's other fixtures.

portfolio.headline: Oracle slides on gas-pipeline delay threatening AI data center buildout
portfolio.body: Oracle shares fell after Energy Transfer's Transwestern Pipeline subsidiary pushed back completion of the Green Chile Project pipeline to February 2027 from a planned August 2026 date. The pipeline is critical fuel-supply infrastructure for Project Jupiter, Oracle's 2.5-gigawatt New Mexico AI data center complex that relies on Bloom Energy fuel cells, stoking investor concern about the pace of Oracle's AI buildout even as Oracle said the broader project ‘remains on schedule,’ per The Motley Fool (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare eases after $2.5B convertible note sale stokes dilution worries
portfolio.body: Cloudflare completed a $2.5 billion offering of zero-coupon convertible senior notes due 2031; despite capped-call protections meant to limit dilution, the raise added fresh caution just days after the company's strong Q2 report and FedRAMP win. Analysts also flagged gross margin compression to about 73%, alongside elevated insider stock sales, per TradingKey (Aug 14) — a pullback from the highs Cloudflare hit after its Q2 beat triggered a wave of Wall Street price-target increases.

portfolio.headline: Figma pressured as 77.7 million shares clear post-earnings lock-up
portfolio.body: Figma's lock-up on 77.7 million Class A shares — about 17% of shares outstanding and roughly 39% of the public float — expired August 7, adding potential new supply on top of last week's post-earnings slide, when the design-software maker guided Q3 revenue growth to 36%, a deceleration from Q2's 48% pace. Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley both trimmed price targets following the report, though the ten-analyst coverage group remains evenly split between buy and hold, per ts2.tech (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike slips into earnings season on profit-taking, insider-sale noise
portfolio.body: CrowdStrike shares fell alongside a broader Nasdaq pullback with no negative fundamental news behind it; the move reflected profit-taking after a strong summer run and pre-earnings positioning ahead of the company's next quarterly report. Investors also parsed CEO George Kurtz's roughly $163.5 million in share sales over the past six months under a pre-set Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, even as sell-side firms including Stifel, UBS and Citigroup kept Buy ratings in place, per QuiverQuant (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: Zoom's fastest growth in 11 quarters overshadowed by soft Q3 outlook
portfolio.body: Zoom Communications posted its best revenue growth in eleven quarters, with Q2 revenue of $1.217 billion (up 4.7% year-over-year) and enterprise revenue up 7%, while AI Companion monthly active users grew more than fourfold year-over-year. But Q3 guidance called for growth of only about 3%, and management said full monetization of new AI products won't arrive until fiscal 2027, tempering enthusiasm for the beat, per coverage of the Q2 report on Yahoo Finance/GuruFocus (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: fuboTV raises EBITDA guidance as North America subscribers hit a record
portfolio.body: fuboTV reported record North America paid subscribers of 5.75 million and a narrower-than-expected quarterly loss, prompting the company to raise the low end of its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90-$100 million from $80-$100 million. New CEO Alisa Bowen pointed to ESPN's ‘Where-to-Watch’ integration under the Disney/Hulu+ Live TV partnership as an emerging subscriber-acquisition channel and promised a broader strategy update on November's earnings call, per Stocktwits (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: Hydrofarm narrows losses but stays in lender talks after Q2 slump
portfolio.body: Hydrofarm's Q2 net sales fell 40.9% to $23.2 million on industry oversupply and discontinued distributed brands, though the net loss narrowed to $10.6 million from $16.9 million a year earlier as gross margin expanded to 11.3%. The cannabis-cultivation supplier applied the $16 million from last month's sale of its Aurora Peat unit toward its $114.4 million term loan and remains under a lender forbearance agreement extended through August 31, per GlobeNewswire (Aug 14/15).

portfolio.headline: Beyond Meat completes 1-for-30 reverse split to save Nasdaq listing
portfolio.body: Beyond Meat's 1-for-30 reverse stock split took effect, consolidating shares to lift its trading level back above Nasdaq's $1 minimum-bid requirement, which it must hold for 10 consecutive sessions before August 31 to avoid delisting. The company also cut its authorized share count from 3 billion to 100 million and adjusted the terms on its outstanding warrants and convertible notes, per Benzinga (Aug 14).

portfolio.headline: C3.ai splits Wall Street as Wedbush's Ives defends Street-high target
portfolio.body: Wedbush's Dan Ives is holding a Street-high price target on C3.ai, betting on the company's early positioning in federal and commercial generative-AI adoption, a shift to consumption-based pricing, and distribution partnerships with Microsoft Azure, AWS and Google Cloud. That view is an outlier: 13 of 14 covering analysts rate the stock Hold or worse after fiscal 2026 revenue fell 36% to $250.3 million and fiscal 2027 guidance of $210-$240 million signaled further contraction, even as founder Thomas Siebel — back as CEO since June — personally bought over 6 million shares and federal bookings grew 134% year-over-year, per 24/7 Wall St. (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Modi marks 80th Independence Day with 'Viksit Bharat' push from Red Fort
stories.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hoisted the flag at Red Fort for his 13th consecutive Independence Day address, unveiling a seven-point growth agenda he called “Shakti ki Sapt Dhara” spanning zero-defect manufacturing, chemical-free farming, defence exports and green hydrogen, urging Indians to have “no more small dreams” as India marks a quarter-century on the road to a developed “Viksit Bharat” by 2047. The ceremony featured a 2,500-cadet rendition of “Vande Mataram” marking 150 years of the anthem, per WION (Aug 15).

stories.headline: Chamoli tunnel disaster: death toll at 7, three still missing
stories.body: Rescue teams battling rising water and low oxygen levels have pulled 12 survivors from the flooded THDC hydropower tunnel in Pipalkoti, Chamoli, with seven bodies recovered and three workers still missing after a landslide near the Birhi river sent water and debris surging into the site. NDRF DIG Mohsen Shahedi said “of the 22 people involved, 12 have been rescued, and seven bodies have been recovered, while three remain missing,” as Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami ordered a magisterial inquiry and Rs 4 lakh compensation per victim's family, per ANI (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Government scraps 20-year-old 12-minute TV ad cap
stories.body: India's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting lifted the two-decade-old rule capping non-programme content, including advertisements, at 12 minutes per hour on television, saying the restriction “had outlived its utility” as channels grew from 62 in 2006 to over 900 while digital platforms faced no such limits. Officials said the sector is “heavily dependent on advertising” and the cap created “a non-level playing field for traditional TV channels vis-à-vis digital media,” per Business Standard (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Delhi locked down with anti-drone shields for Independence Day
stories.body: Delhi Police screened more than 20,000 residents and workers around Red Fort and deployed anti-drone shields ahead of the 80th Independence Day, shutting Chandni Chowk roads from 4am to 11am and diverting DTC buses. DCP (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said “extensive security measures have been implemented in and around the Red Fort, which is considered one of the most sensitive locations,” per India.com (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Farage reclaims Clacton seat in record-field by-election
stories.body: Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election with 22,239 votes, comfortably beating satirical rival Count Binface's 9,455 among 35 candidates, on a reduced 44% turnout after Labour and the Conservatives boycotted the contest as a “political stunt.” Farage, who quit as MP in July amid scrutiny of an undisclosed £5 million cryptocurrency donation, skipped the count and cancelled his victory speech, saying he “wanted the people of Clacton to be my judge, not the mainstream media,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 14).

stories.headline: NHS transplant chief accuses leadership of tolerating 'unfair' waits
stories.body: Professor Derek Manas, medical director of NHS Blood and Transplant, rebuked NHS England for a fragmented system with “few consequences for poor performance,” noting heart and lung transplant numbers have stagnated for 30 years and Britain transplants just one in seven donated hearts and one in ten donated lungs. He said heart-transplant waits now range from eight months to four and a half years, with half of the UK's six heart/lung transplant centres losing their lead surgeon within two years, per AOL/PA (Aug 13).

stories.headline: PM Burnham signals more business-rates relief at October budget
stories.body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he intends to widen business-rates relief for high street firms beyond the pub sector at the 28 October budget, saying “we're going to look at business rates more broadly for high street businesses in the budget, so there's plenty more that we can do.” He cautioned he “won't bring forward things that I can't fully fund,” while acknowledging “the cost of doing business is too high” after prior national insurance hikes on employers, per The Industry.fashion (Aug 12).

stories.headline: Oman oil spill spreads to 1,300 sq km as salvage crews board tanker
stories.body: British risk firm Ambrey said personnel have boarded the grounded, Russian-linked tanker Caroline Bezengi off Oman's Hallaniyat archipelago to begin stabilising its cargo as oil reached beaches along the central coast. Greenpeace said the slick has ballooned from 45 sq km in late July to roughly 1,300 sq km by August 13, far above Oman's earlier 400 sq km estimate; Ambrey director Ed Wollaston said crews “are working around the clock to mitigate the environmental impact,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 14).

stories.headline: GCC condemns Iranian strikes on two Emirati tankers in Hormuz
stories.body: GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi denounced Iran's attacks on two ADNOC tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz as “a dangerous and unacceptable escalation” and “a direct threat to the security and safety of maritime navigation,” accusing Tehran of trying to weaponise “this vital international waterway.” The bloc pledged “full and unwavering solidarity with the UAE,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Saudi-led Red Sea naval coalition, with Qatar aboard, goes operational
stories.body: A 13-nation maritime alliance led by Saudi Arabia to protect shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb, Red Sea and Gulf of Aden from Houthi attacks became operational on August 13 after its third meeting in Jeddah, with Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Egypt and Pakistan among the members under commander Rear Admiral Abdullah bin Salem Al-Shehri. Analyst Ahmed Nagi of the International Crisis Group said the pact “could become important if it is able to turn agreements and political commitments into concrete action,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 14).

stories.headline: Doha real estate posts QR353m in weekly deals
stories.body: Qatar's property market recorded QR353 million in transactions in the first week of August, led by Doha Municipality with 42 deals and Lusail with 10 residential sales worth QR10 million, while outlying municipalities like Al Shamal saw just a single transaction. Officials said “the high volume of deals in Doha highlights the region's enduring appeal to investors and buyers who continue to prioritise established urban centres,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 14).

doha_events.headline: Liwan × M7 Kid's Summer Camp
doha_events.body: A hands-on creative summer camp for kids at M7 and Liwan, running in two week-long sessions (Aug 9–13 and Aug 16–20, 2026) from 10am–1pm daily; per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Spinning Art Label Design Lab
doha_events.body: A free drop-in workshop for adults at the MIA Library, Museum of Islamic Art, running through August 31, 2026 during regular library hours; per Qatar Living's weekly roundup.

doha_events.headline: Ladies Sport Night: Summer Edition
doha_events.body: A free weekly women's fitness evening at Education City, Gate 35, held every Tuesday from 4pm–8pm through the summer; registration required, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Snoonu City × Fit Island Tuesday Run
doha_events.body: A free community run at Aspire Dome held every Tuesday at 7:30pm, part of the ongoing Fit Island summer programming, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Pizza Masterclass at Adrift Anda
doha_events.body: A hands-on pizza-making class for kids at Adrift Anda by David Myers, Le Royal Méridien Place Vendôme Lusail, held Thursdays and Fridays from 3pm–5pm; per Qatar Living.
